source.title: The Multiplicative Noise in Stochastic Gradient Descent: Data-Dependent Regularization, Continuous and Discrete Approximation
source.authors: Jing-Feng Wu; Wen-Qing Hu; Haoyi Xiong; Jun Huan; Zhan-Xing Zhu

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares small- and large-batch training and reports that its added compensatory noise can close the large-batch generalization gap. This refines the scope of V5; it does not test fixed-epoch comparisons.
record.gate_note: Only V5 is tested. The study reports test accuracy for large-batch SGD and mini-batch MSGD comparisons. Its theory and experiments about noise classes do not test the other claim versions. Figure values are transcribed from the paper's text-rendered figure labels.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5's recipe-adaptation component: compensatory sampling noise restores large-batch test accuracy. Its comparisons hold iterations, rather than epochs, fixed, so they do not establish V5's fixed-epoch penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that noise class is not crucial given suitable magnitude and covariance, and that compensatory sampling noise closes the large-batch generalization gap in their experiments. This does not establish recovery within a matched epoch budget.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds sampling noise through MSGD and compares it with SGD; its large-batch experiments do not report fixed-epoch controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and the addition of compensatory sampling noise change reported test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Different noise distribution classes can yield similar generalization when noise magnitude and covariance are suitable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise distribution class need not determine gradient-noise regularization when magnitude and covariance are controlled.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 108, 2020
record.problems: Large-batch results are shown as test accuracy over iterations, not under a stated fixed-epoch budget. The excerpted figure labels give endpoint accuracies but no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Other figure-labeled comparisons, including SVHN and FashionMNIST, and Figure 1's noise-class comparisons were not included because they are not needed to represent V5's large-batch effect and compensation. Figure 2(a) SVHN and Figure 2(b) CIFAR-10 without augmentation are included only insofar as represented by R1–R5.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Matched fixed-epoch penalties or recovery; workload-dependent thresholds; language models; longer-training interventions; learning-rate scaling with warmup; isolated effects of normalization or regularization changes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings and correlations with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: CIFAR-100 ResNet-18 results: SGD-500 76.38%, SGD-2k 72.78%, MSGD-Fisher-2k 76.83%, SGD-5k 59.16%, MSGD-Fisher-5k 76.46%. These extend both the batch penalty and its recovery to another dataset and are not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded accuracies match Figure 2. Recovery supports V5's existing adaptation clause rather than requiring a new scope limitation. The unmodified-SGD results cannot independently support the fixed-epoch clause. Other figure comparisons are broadly declared in rows_left_out; Table 1 is not.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Widening beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of optimizer tuning.

Fixed-epoch comparisons; workload-dependent batch-size thresholds; language models; learning-rate scaling with warmup; and the effects of normalization or regularization changes as separate interventions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18, CIFAR-10 without augmentation or weight decay; tuned compensatory noise at batches 1k and 2k, matched iterations
relationships.reason: R4–R5 restore accuracy to 85.88% and 85.75%, versus 85.51% for small-batch SGD, supporting recipe-dependent recovery; fixed-epoch recovery remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest compensatory noise restored small-batch accuracy without augmentation or weight decay under matched iterations.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18, CIFAR-10 with augmentation and weight decay; tuned compensatory noise at batches 2k and 5k, matched iterations
relationships.reason: R9–R10 reach 95.26% and 95.18%, versus 95.12% for small-batch SGD, supporting recipe-dependent recovery; this already fits V5's adaptation qualification.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest compensatory noise matched or slightly exceeded small-batch accuracy with augmentation and weight decay under matched iterations.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18, CIFAR-100; large-batch compensatory noise with the Figure 2(c) setup
relationships.reason: Text-only verdict pending missing rows: Table 1 reports 76.83% and 76.46% with compensation versus 76.38% for batch-500 SGD; unmodified large batches reach 72.78% and 59.16%.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest compensatory noise improved larger-batch CIFAR-100 accuracy beyond the batch-500 reference.
